theory.title: Talking about sport, exercise and routines
theory.explanation: Use play with ball games and team sports (play football), go with activities ending in -ing (go swimming), and do with exercise or martial arts (do yoga). Use the present simple to describe routines. Put frequency adverbs before most verbs: I usually go running. Ask How often...? to ask about frequency. Use can/can't + base verb to talk about ability.
theory.tip: Remember the collocations: play tennis, go cycling, do exercise. In the third person singular, add -s: She plays basketball.

patterns.label: Block 1 · Play + sport
patterns.pattern: play + ball game or team sport

patterns.label: Block 2 · Go + -ing
examples: He goes cycling at the weekend.

patterns.label: Block 3 · Do + activity
examples: I do yoga in the morning.
She does gymnastics twice a week.

patterns.label: Block 5 · Frequency adverbs
examples: We usually walk to the gym.

patterns.label: Block 7 · Time expressions
patterns.pattern: every day / once a week / twice a month
examples: I go running twice a week.

items.prompt: My brother ___ swimming twice a week.
They ___ go to the gym on Mondays.

content.passage: At Riverside Sports Centre, people of all ages enjoy being active. The centre opens at seven every morning. Before work, some people go swimming or use the gym. After school, children play basketball and badminton. My friend Leo plays football twice a week, but he doesn't enjoy running. I usually do yoga on Wednesdays and go cycling at the weekend. The centre also has a small café where visitors can buy water and healthy snacks. You can join a beginner's class if you can't play a sport yet. The coaches are friendly and help everyone learn. Exercise is a good way to stay fit, meet people and have fun.

content.audioTranscript: Welcome to the Green Street Sports Club. Our doors open at eight on weekdays and at nine at the weekend. You can play basketball in the main hall, or go swimming in our indoor pool. We have yoga classes on Tuesdays and Thursdays. The beginners' running group meets every Monday at half past six. You should bring a bottle of water and comfortable trainers. Our coach, Sarah, can help you learn a new sport. The football team trains twice a week. If you can't play yet, don't worry: you can join our beginner class. After exercise, you can relax in the café and buy a healthy snack. Ask at reception for a membership card.
